history.period: Several hundred years old per local belief; exact period unknown; legend associates it with Prithviraj Chauhan (12th century)
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple at Shahganj on the Fatehpur Sikri (Jaipur) road, one of the four Shiva temples at the four corners of Agra. Legend says ruler Prithviraj Chauhan was passing through what was then forest; his horse repeatedly came loose, and he discovered a shivling tied at the root of a tree — he built the temple there. Another tradition links it to the Dvapara Yuga, saying the shivling appeared from the womb of the earth. The exact age of the deity is unknown. The complex, resembling an old village residence protected from surrounding urbanisation, has a Nandi statue in the courtyard, an ancient well, a dharamshala, and Nagara-style shikhara architecture with carved pillars and gateways. Note: TripAdvisor and srimandir publish different opening hours — verify.

name: Prithvinath Temple
town_description: Agra, on the banks of the Yamuna in western Uttar Pradesh, was the capital of the Mughal Empire under Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan, and is home to the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri. Alongside its Mughal monuments it is an old Hindu pilgrimage centre, guarded — in local belief — by four ancient Shiva temples set at the four corners of the city.
